A video showing a massive fire near a temple is being shared on social media (here, here, and here) with the claim that Muslims set fire to the temple in Bangladesh. Let’s verify the truth behind the video in this article.
Claim: The video shows a temple in Bangladesh engulfed in flames after Muslims burned it down.
Fact: The viral video does not show a temple in Bangladesh being set on fire by Muslims. In fact, it shows a fire at a plastic warehouse near Kukra Chowk in the New Mandi police station area of Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, on 21 November 2026. The fire reportedly broke out after sparks from fireworks during a wedding ceremony reached the warehouse. The location was geolocated to Kukra Chowk, Muzaffarnagar, by matching the surrounding structures and landmarks visible in the viral video with those at the site. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to multiple social media posts (here, here) dated 21 November 2026 featuring the same video. According to these posts, the video shows a massive fire at a warehouse near Kukra Chowk in the New Mandi police station area of Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh. The fire reportedly triggered panic among nearby shopkeepers and residents, while several fire engines rushed to the spot to extinguish it.
Using clues from these social media posts, we searched relevant keywords and found several news reports (here, here, and here) with the same visuals. According to these reports, a massive fire broke out at a plastic warehouse near Kukra Chowk in the New Mandi police station area of Muzaffarnagar on 21 November 2026. The fire reportedly started when sparks from fireworks set off during a wedding ceremony, particularly during the bride’s farewell, reached the warehouse. Eleven fire engines and water tankers from nearby factories were deployed to extinguish the blaze, which took over five hours to bring under control. The fire caused panic among nearby shopkeepers, prompting the evacuation of surrounding shops. The warehouse reportedly stored crockery used for wedding ceremonies, and the owner said the fire caused significant losses. Officials said the cause was based on accounts from residents, while the extent of the damage was yet to be assessed.
We also geolocated the incident to Kukra Chowk, Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh. The surrounding structures and landmarks visible in the viral video match those at the location. The comparison can be seen below.
To sum up, a video of a warehouse fire accident in U.P is falsely shared as Muslims burning a temple in Bangladesh.

In November, a video (archived) circulated that social media users claimed authentically shows a group of Muslims calling themselves "Soldiers of Allah" and demanding Shariah be put in place in Manchester, England.
According to the Council on Foreign Relations, a U.S. foreign policy think tank, Shariah is "the divine counsel that Muslims follow to live moral lives and grow close to God." Interpretations of Shariah, the principles of which stem from the Quran and hadith, the latter of which are sayings attributed to the Prophet Muhammad, form the basis of Islamic law.
The video in question shows people gathered on Wilmslow Road in Rusholme, south of Manchester, a stretch of road that is also known as the "Curry Mile" for its large number of restaurants specializing in South Asian and Middle Eastern food. The footage shows large groups of people, who appeared to be majority male, chanting and beating their chests.
One Instagram user who shared the video wrote:
A large group of military-age men took to the streets in a Manchester suburb calling themselves soldiers of Allah and demanding sharia law be put in place because they now form the majority in the neighborhood. The march was open and organized, not a quiet gathering. When a neighborhood shifts demographically and then the new majority starts openly calling for a different legal system, the question is how far that demand is expected to go. Local officials and residents are left deciding whether this is just free expression or the start of parallel rules. Do you think this is being handled the right way in the UK?
The footage also circulated on Facebook (archived). Snopes readers searched our site for information about the clips.
The video appears authentic, meaning it shows an event that actually happened and wasn't created used artificial intelligence. However, people who shared in it November miscaptioned the footage.
It doesn't show Muslims calling themselves "Soldiers of Allah" or calling for Shariah in the U.K. Rather, the videos show Shiite Muslims marking Ashura, the culmination of 10 days of mourning to mark the martyrdom of Husayn ibn Ali, the grandson of the prophet Muhammad, on June 21.
According to the Encyclopedia Britannica, Shiite Muslims mark this day with assemblies such as the one seen in the video that feature, "sermons, poetry, chest-beating, and passion plays reenacting Husayn's martyrdom."
The Ashura assembly on the "Curry Mile" is an annual event in Manchester that local news media has covered for more than 10 years. The Manchester Evening news called the event a "ritual self-flagellation procession" in 2015 but did not report that the people participating called themselves "Soldiers of Allah" or demanded Shariah be imposed in the U.K.
The source of the video that circulated in November was unclear, though at least two of the clips featured (at 0:06 and 0:16) camefrom a separate video (at 1:20 and 1:59, archived) posted on Instagram by 
Murtaza Ali Shah, a journalist for a Pakistani news outlet.
Shah confirmed to Snopes via Instagram he recorded the footage and it showed the Ashura event in Manchester in June.
In addition to misrepresenting what the video showed, the social media post above also made a false claim about the alleged "Soldiers of Allah" calling for Shariah in the U.K.
The poster wrote (emphasis ours): "A large group of military-age men took to the streets in a Manchester suburb calling themselves soldiers of Allah and demanding sharia law be put in place because they now form the majority in the neighborhood."
Manchester, where the June Ashura assembly took place, is not majority Muslim. According to the latest U.K. Ccensus data from 2021, 22.3% of people — less than one in four — within the Manchester City Council governance area identified as Muslims. Rusholme, where the "Curry Mile" is located, is part of Manchester City Council. According to census data, 38.5% of people in the Rusholme East census area, which borders the "Curry Mile," identified as Muslim.
For further reading, Snopes previously investigated whether a video showed U.K. shoppers standing in gender-segregated lines and another video of Shiite Muslims marking Ashura in Dearborn, Michigan.

“We’ve received an extremely high volume of messages due to multiple providers in our area retiring or leaving their practice very recently,” the woman’s voice said with a hint of exasperation, “so please understand it may take longer than normal to receive a return call back.”

Two attacks in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) have killed 4 workers responding to the Ebola outbreak and injured 5 others.
The attacks occurred overnight on a shared living camp in Biakato Mines and an Ebola response coordination office in Mangina.
“We are heartbroken that people have died in the line of duty as they worked to save others,” said Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, World Health Organization Director-General. “The world has lost brave professionals.”
The dead include a member of a vaccination team, two drivers and a police officer. No WHO staff are among those killed, one staff member was injured.
“My heart goes out to the family and friends of the first responders killed in these attacks,” said Dr Matshidiso Moeti, WHO Regional Director for Africa. “We are doing everything possible to bring the injured and front-line workers in the impacted areas to safety. These constant attacks must stop. We will continue to work with the DRC Government, partners and MONUSCO to ensure the security of our staff and other health workers.”
In the last week, there were 7 cases of Ebola, down from a peak of over 120 per week in April 2019.
“Ebola was retreating. These attacks will give it force again, and more people will die as a consequence,” said Dr Tedros. “It will be tragic to see more unnecessary suffering in communities that have already suffered so much. We call on everyone who has a role to play to end this cycle of violence.”
The situation is still evolving. WHO will provide updates as new information comes in.

Parts of Bangladesh were shut down Thursday as protests by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina sparked clashes, bomb blasts and arson attacks, with the ancestral home of former leader Muhammad Yunus set ablaze in the violence.
Hasina’s Awami League party had called for a week-long programme of protests and rallies to mobilise support for Hasina’s planned return in December, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on Thursday.
Hasina, who has lived in exile in neighbouring India since she fled Dhaka following violent protests demanding her resignation in August 2024, has requested a new passport and identity card to facilitate her return. Her supporters are protesting against the government’s rejection of that request.
To deter violence, 97 platoons of the Bangladesh Border Guard fanned out across seven districts, including Gopalganj and Faridpur, considered to have many Hasina supporters, a spokesperson said.
Police said former interim leader Yunus’ ancestral home in Chattogram, about 300km (186 miles) south-east of Dhaka, was set on fire late on Wednesday.
It is likely that flammable substances were thrown into an unused ground-floor room, police told Reuters, adding that Yunus’ paternal family members, who live on the upper floors, are safe.
Reuters could not immediately reach the Yunus Centre thinktank that speaks on his behalf to seek comment. Yunus and his government, which led Bangladesh after Hasina’s ouster, have faced hostility from her supporters.
During the last 10 days of protests, police have reported dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of vehicles being set afire in at least 28 districts, injuring several police officials and members of the public, media have said.
Late on Tuesday, an activist of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist party (BNP) was allegedly killed by unidentified people during a protest near Hasina’s home district of Gopalganj, police said.
On the same night, a crude bomb exploded outside the Dhaka residence of cultural affairs minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury, and the house of a BNP lawmaker and shops belonging to BNP supporters in Gopalganj were set on fire, police added.
On Wednesday morning, a bus company helper was burnt to death in the southern district of Pirojpur after two buses were set on fire, authorities said.
Tuesday marks a year since Hasina was sentenced to death by a local court that found her guilty of ordering a deadly crackdown on a student-led uprising against her in 2024. She has lived in exile in neighbouring India since fleeing Dhaka.
On Thursday, authorities detained former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid, who faces charges over several killings during the 2024 protests, from his house in Dhaka, police told Reuters.
At least 37 branches and offices of Grameen Bank, set up by Yunus, have been targeted in arson attacks or attempted fires since 10 November, with 14 more attacked since midnight on Tuesday, the bank said.
On Tuesday, the home minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused Awami League leaders abroad of inciting supporters to destabilise Bangladesh and torch property, adding that those involved in violence would be identified and prosecuted.
Awami League leaders, most of them in hiding, could not be reached for comment.

Zelensky compares Trump cosying up to Putin to being friends with Hitler in the Second World War: ‘He’s a killer’
The US president has deepened Washington’s ties with Moscow since taking office in January 2025

Volodymyr Zelensky has hit out at Donald Trump for cosying up to Russian president Vladimir Putin - comparing it to befriending Adolf Hitler during the Second World War.
The Ukrainian president discussed a photo of the Russian and US leaders posted by Trump in which he described the Russian president as “my friend”. A video of the same meeting in Shenzhen, China, earlier this month showed Trump jokingly saying “who is he?” before entering the room and giving Putin a hug.
"Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky told the BBC in an interview in Kyiv.
"He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be. It’s the same if somebody said about Hitler during the Second World War that he is a good friend,” he continued. “No, he’s not a friend.”
The meeting has sparked further concern among Europe and Nato, appearing to be another development in the warming of relations between Washington and Moscow.
Trump’s attitude to Zelensky has been far more dismissive, at times hostile and deeply critical of the Ukrainian president, who he has previously blamed for the war which was started by Russia in February 2022.
Recent attempts by peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff have made little progress in forcing Moscow into agreeing a ceasefire, but they have suggested that Washington appears to be more aligned with Moscow than with Kyiv.
Kushner, who is also Donald Trump’s son-in-law, accused Europe of having “no plan” to end the war, and said negotiations should focus on the post-war period rather than looking at an immediate ceasefire. The Kremlin has argued the same.
The US envoy was also been accused of being like Putin’s “spokesman” after showering the Russian president with praise in an interview with Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner.
“Going into the meetings, President Putin is very organised. People can like what he’s done, they can not like what he’s done, but he’s definitely a grand master of politics,” Kushner said in the interview.
Maria Popova, director of the Jean Monnet Centre Montreal who focusses on the Russia-Ukraine war, said on X, said Kushner spoke “as if he’s Putin’s spokesman rather than a mediator or a US envoy”.
Zelensky, in his interview, made a similar criticism of the US president.
“They have to pressure the situation,” he said. “The situation is that Russia is the aggressor. That’s why they’re mediators, it’s not about comfortable talks, it’s about a strong country who can pressure because this country has power and respect.”
He added: “We need the American position to be the American position. We don’t need signals from the United States which we can get from Russia,” he said.
Asked if the US is pressuring Russia as much as he would like them to, the Ukrainian president added: “No, no of course.”

The 2026-27 Indian Women’s League match between East Bengal and NITA FA has been postponed for the second time, the league announced on Friday.
The fixture was rescheduled for Sunday, November 29, with a kickoff time of 7pm IST.
“The revised date and kick-off time are yet to be confirmed. Further updates regarding the rescheduling of the fixture will be shared in due course,” the league said in a statement.

East Bengal is playing Garhwal United on Friday, which would leave them with just a day’s gap between the two fixtures. Meanwhile, NITA, which clinched a 5-0 win over debutant Juba Sangha earlier on Friday, would also have a day’s time.
The Moshal Girls have won both their matches so far, 1-0 victories over Gokulam Kerala and Kickstart. On the other hand, NITA too has been unbeaten so far, notching up wins against Garhwal and now Juba Sangha.

Delhi AQI today: A smoky haze covered the national capital on Friday, November 27, as the air quality index (AQI) hovered in the 'severe' category at 273 at 6:11 AM. It fell nearly 120 points from the overnight peak of 393, recorded at 2:00 AM. As of Friday, New Delhi ranked 46th among the world's most polluted cities. Delhi's air quality improved through Thursday afternoon before worsening again in the evening. The AQI fell to 121 at 5:01 PM, its lowest reading in the previous 24 hours. It rose above 300 around 8:00 PM and reached 393 at 2:01 AM on the intervening night of Thursday and Friday. Readings remained above 300 until after 5 AM before easing later in the morning, according to AQI.in. Delhi's seven-day AQI peaked at 465 at 6 AM on November 20. The seven-day period ended on November 26. The lowest reading in that series was 170 at noon on November 26. Early morning readings generally hovered between 350 and 450 on several days during that period. At 6:11 AM on Friday, Delhi's PM10 level stood at 274 micrograms per cubic metre, compared with the World Health Organization's guideline of 45 micrograms per cubic metre. Carbon monoxide was reported at 2,208 parts per billion (ppb), while nitrogen dioxide measured 23 parts per billion and sulphur dioxide nine parts per billion. Ozone was recorded at two parts per billion. The temperature was 14 degrees Celsius, humidity stood at 57%, wind speed was 3.6 km/h, and the UV index was zero. According to PTI, citing data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), Delhi's air quality was in the 'poor' category on Thursday, extending its streak of poor air quality days, with the AQI settling at 224. Of the 55 monitoring stations across the capital, at least 40 were in the 'poor' category, 14 in the 'moderate' category, and one in the 'very poor' category. The monitoring station at ITO recorded 'very poor' air quality. The CPCB data also showed that Thursday was the 12th consecutive day when the national capital recorded 'poor' air quality. On Tuesday, Delhi's AQI was 227. It later declined to 220 on Wednesday before rising to 224 on Thursday. PTI, citing real-time source apportionment estimates for Delhi on Thursday, noted that secondary organic aerosols were the largest contributors to PM2.5 pollution, accounting for roughly 24.8% of the estimated load. These aerosols form in the atmosphere when gases released by sources such as vehicles, industries and other combustion activities react with other compounds in the air to produce fine particles. Vehicular emissions accounted for 20.6% of the total. Biomass burning contributed 19.7%, while secondary inorganic pollutants made up 12.5%. Other sources included waste burning (11.4%), road dust, soil and minerals (4.5%), industrial activity (2.7%), coal burning (1.6%), firecrackers (1.4%), and mixed combustion (0.6%). Between October 1 and November 25, Delhi ranked first among the 10 most polluted cities in the National Capital Region (NCR) in terms of both PM2.5 and PM10 levels. It reportedly moved up from third and fourth positions, respectively, during the corresponding period last year. An analysis of the India Air Quality Portal by EnviroCatalysts found that Delhi recorded the highest average PM2.5 concentration at 113 micrograms per cubic metre during the period under review. Gurugram followed with 109 micrograms per cubic metre, while Noida and Ghaziabad recorded 105 and 103, respectively. Meerut reported 96, Baghpat and Greater Noida 95 each, Panipat 90, Bulandshahr 82 and Faridabad 69 micrograms per cubic metre. The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) classifies an Air Quality Index (AQI) reading of 0-50 as 'good', 51-100 as 'satisfactory', 101-200 as 'moderate', 201-300 as 'poor', 301-400 as 'very poor' and 401-500 as 'severe'. AQI.in follows the US AQI scale, under which readings of 0-50 are classified as 'good', 51-100 as 'moderate', 101-150 as 'poor', 151-200 as 'unhealthy', 201-300 as 'severe ', and 301 and above as 'hazardous'. From its origins as a racing game called Race ‘n’ Chase to billion-dollar sales records, GTA has a fascinating history. Here are 11 surprising facts about the franchise, including Hollywood connections, hidden ghosts, clever anti-piracy tricks, celebrity lawsuits, and its Scottish roots.
After more than a decade of waiting, Rockstar Games has finally launched perhaps the most anticipated game in the recent history of gaming. Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6). It has been barely a few days since the game hit the stands and the Web, and it already has the world (gaming and non-gaming too) in its grip, and is setting sales records.
Its release means saying goodbye to the legendary “we got (this/something) before GTA 6” meme, but GTA 6 is already carving a place for itself in the franchise’s history, a history marked by crime, cars, and chaos and a lot of other things that even diehard fans might not be aware of.
From celebrity lawsuits to ghosts and many controversies, the world of GTA is filled with insane stories. So even as you set yourself up for another session of GTA 6 or wait for your copy of the game to download, or just turn your nose up at “crazy gamers who will line up for anything”, here are eleven amazing facts you might not know (but should know) about the legendary Grand Theft Auto franchise.
Table of Contents
It was originally supposed to be a racing game (and called Race’n’Chase)
It may look completely different today, but GTA was originally supposed to be a fast-paced, addictive racing game called “Race ‘n’ Chase.” Development of the game got underway in the mid-nineties, but the developers did not quite get things right. Early models had car-crashing issues and coding glitches that made police cars ram into player cars aggressively, instead of just chasing them. This, of course, took away its traditional racing game feel. But during testing, players enjoyed this glitch and chaos, so the developers decided to move away from a “Race n Chase” sort of setup and decided to create an open world action-oriented game. They called it Grand Theft Auto (GTA). The rest, as they love to say, is history.
Play the OG GTA online and free of cost
Want to experience the original Grand Theft Auto that was released in 1997? Well, you can actually play it for free online in a browser at https://www.playdosgames.com/online/grand-theft-auto/. Just make sure you have a keyboard handy, as it struggles with touch controls.
Thank you, Tony Montana! GTA: Vice City was inspired by Scarface!
Even the greatest video games have to draw inspiration from somewhere, and in the case of GTA: Vice City, inspiration came from Brian De Palma’s 1983 crime classic, Scarface. The developers used the movie as a blueprint to showcase how Miami looked back in the 80s. The protagonist in the game also follows a very similar arc to the protagonist in the film, the iconic Tony Montana, and even has a location similar to that of Tony Montana’s (Scarface’s protagonist) infamous mansion in it.
GTA has a lot of Hollywood in it…but is not too fond of stars
GTA has not just drawn inspiration from Hollywood, but has also featured many famous actors from it. The game has cast a number of actors, comedians, and musicians to either play themselves or voice a character. A key reason for hiring musicians and comedians to play themselves in the game or be a part of an extensive radio or DJ set is to make the city in the game feel even more real and lived in. Famous actors like Ray Liotta, Samuel L. Jackson, Burt Reynolds, and many more have been a part of the franchise. This tradition lives on with GTA 6, as this time around actors Dylan Rourke and Manni Perez have voiced the two leads of the game.
That said, problems with a number of high-profile stars (most notably Burt Reynolds) led Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser to say in an interview with Vulture “We don’t bring in name actors anymore because of their egos and, most important of all, because we believe we get a better sense of immersion using talented actors whose voices you don’t recognize.”
The Ghost Town of GTA 3 that is ‘out of bounds’
Imagine having a small part of the game that you cannot explore? Well, that is exactly what the Ghost Town in GTA 3 is. It has nothing to do with gameplay, lacks the general collision mechanism of the game, and yet it exists. The ‘out of bounds’ area was actually designed as part of GTA 3’s opening cinematics and was put away from the main map, and kept in the game only for the intro scene. However, players found their way to the location using glitches and modifications, although they could not interact with it like the rest of the game. Before Vice City, there was Ghost City in the GTAverse.
Punishing pirates, the GTA way
By the time GTA 4 was released in 2008, the GTA franchise had become insanely famous. And with great celebrity and terrific sales comes…great piracy. As pirated and unauthorized units of the game became a problem, Rockstar Games used some very creative countermeasures to punish/ annoy those who bought pirated copies of the game. Unauthorized copies ended up with constant drunk effects on the camera, sudden and auto acceleration, broken mission scripts, damaged cars, and more, which were put in place to make the pirated game actually feel pirated. You do not pirate a gangster game easily!
Macabre and moving Easter eggs
The GTA franchise is laden with Easter eggs, but two of the most amazing ones are found in GTA 5. What makes them special is the attention to both detail and sentiment. These are not your run-of-the-mill “press this key and your car changes into Superman” or “use this key combo to start driving on Mars” kinds of easter eggs, but much more somber and sensitive ones.
In GTA 5 between 23:00 and 00:00, you can actually find a translucent figure at the peak of Mount Gordo. There is a flat rock where the ghost of “Jolene Cranley-Evans,” who was said to have been killed by her husband, Jock Cranley, appears around midnight. Jock had pushed her off the mountain peak, which is also why, when the player goes near the ghost, it disappears and “Jock” written in blood appears on the flat rock!
The other Easter egg is not as eerie but definitely heartbreaking. A small dog can be seen sitting quietly next to the grave of his owner in the Pacific Bluffs cemetery between 10:00 am and 11:00 am. This is the game paying tribute to a real grieving dog, Greyfriars Bobby, a 19th-century dog who guarded his owner’s grave for 14 years.
Watch the moon in GTA 5!
It was not just the easter eggs that were amazing in GTA 5. Rockstar Games upped their detail game (pun intended) by several notches, paying attention to the tiniest of details. The best example of this is the moon in the game. Yes, the moon. The moon in GTA 5 does not remain the same through the gameplay and actually goes through proper lunar phases– something many players might not even notice during regular gameplay. So you get full, crescent, waxing gibbous, and other phases of the moon while playing the game. Now, that’s one moonshot that worked.
GTA and controversies go hand in hand, and even the Guinness Book agrees
Ever since its release in 1997, the GTA franchise has been surrounded by controversies. And these have only gotten bigger with each new version. Celebrities like Lindsay Lohan, Karen Gravano, Michael Washington have filed lawsuits against Rockstar Games’ parent company Take-Two Interactive, for modeling its characters on them.
The game has also attracted a lot of criticism for its alleged glorification of violence and sexual themes – GTA: San Andreas was hit by the Hot Coffee controversy in 2004, when developers left explicit, sexual interactive code in the game instead of deleting it. They had disabled the code, but players used mods to access it, which allowed them to make the main character (CJ) have sexual encounters with characters after inviting them for coffee. The franchise had over 4,000 news stories published in July 2008, all related to violence, crime and misogyny perpetration. It is hardly surprising that it has been recognized as the most controversial video game franchise in history by Guinness World Records. Of course, millions still love it. But that is another story…
Generating the kind of revenues that make Hollywood envious
GTA games generate the kind of revenue that Hollywood blockbusters can only dream of. GTA 5 hit one billion USD in retail sales within three days, making it the fastest entertainment property overall to hit that milestone at that time. And GTA 6 seems to have followed in its footsteps. While no official figures have been released, it is estimated that nearly 25 million copies of the game were sold on the first day, and its earnings come to around 3.8 billion USD. Just for context, Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey has made USD 1.8 billion at the box office at the time of writing.
It is made in Scotland!
It might be released by a US company (Rockstar Games) and might feature US cities in its gameplay, but Grand Theft Auto is actually made in Edinburgh, Scotland, by Rockstar North, which was previously known as DMA Design, a company that was incorporated in Dublin. So yes, believe it or not, the game that many consider to be classically all-American was actually made by the Brits. And that too, by the ones that wear kilts. Bravehearts, truly.

NBC has pulled an ad from a Middle East advocacy organization that calls for the end of U.S. military aid to Israel. The network will review its ad approval procedures after criticism from the Simon Wiesenthal Center and other organizations.
The spot, purchased by the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project, pushes for the end of U.S. military aid to Israel amid the humanitarian crisis in Gaza. The spot titled “Every Three Seconds” ran Nov. 25 on NBC in primetime during the network’s “Saturday Night Live” Thanksgiving special.
The ad makes a jarring juxtaposition between the suffering in Gaza and scenes of a typical American preteen girl doing chores and odd jobs to save money for a bicycle amid tough economic times. Just as the American girl brings her jar full of money into a bike shop, the spot cuts to a scene of a girl standing in a pile of rubble in Gaza. As the camera pans back, the girl is revealed to be leaning on a crutch, having lost one of her lower legs. The spot tells viewers that “Every three seconds” the U.S. sends about $400 million in military aid to Israel under a long-term deal set to expire in 2028.
NBC’s top brass were unaware of the spot before it aired. As a result, there will be a review of the network’s ad approval processes, according to a person familiar with the situation.
Jim Berk, CEO of the Wiesenthal Center, issued a lengthy statement on Thursday questioning NBC’s decision to air the ad during an “SNL” entertainment special in primetime. He pointed to the ad’s potential to fuel hostility against Israel and Jews.
“The advertisement’s imagery, an American child’s hardship set against the anguish of a child in Gaza, offers viewers a seductive but unsubstantiated narrative: that the struggles of American families are somehow bound up with U.S. support for Israel,” Berk stated. “In collapsing a complex foreign policy into a single, emotionally charged image, it erases the deeper realities, including the imperative to protect Israeli lives and the very existence of the country itself. By manipulating emotion and stripping it of context, this ad seeks to become a catalyst for hostility. … Without scrutiny, insinuations and half-truths are allowed to seep into the consciousness of millions, unchallenged and unchecked. Turning children’s suffering into a prop for political theater is an unacceptable manipulation.”
The Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project did not immediately respond to a request for comment on NBC’s decision. It’s unclear how many more times the spot had been scheduled to run on NBCUniversal platforms. According to the organization’s website, IMEU “was founded in 2005 by a group of concerned Americans who want to foster an increased understanding among Americans about Palestine and the Palestinians.”

Delimitation Bill proposes formation of commission, SC judge, CEC nominee among members
The panel will be formed if the Bill passes both Houses of Parliament and becomes an Act with the President's assent.
A delimitation commission will be immediately constituted after The Delimitation (Second) Bill takes effect, according to a copy of the document accessed by HT.
According to the document, the proposed three-member delimitation commission will include a serving or former Supreme Court judge, the Chief Election Commissioner or one of the Election Commissioners (ex-officio) appointed by him and a state election commissioner.
Section 3 of the Bill provides for the constitution of a delimitation commission. Here's what it reads:
Deep Dive
“(a) one member, who shall be a person who is or has been a Judge of the Supreme Court, to be appointed by the Central Government, as the Chairperson of the Commission; (b) the Chief Election Commissioner or an Election Commissioner nominated by the Chief Election Commissioner, ex officio: ….. and (c) the State Election Commissioner of the State concerned, ex officio.”
The proposed Bill, which is expected to be introduced in the Lok Sabha during the special Parliament sitting scheduled from November 30, says that the panel will be formed if the Bill passes both Houses of Parliament and becomes an Act with the President's assent.
Also Read | Govt’s delimitation plan: 50% seat hike for every state, Lok Sabha strength ceiling rises to 850
A serving or former Supreme Court judge will be appointed as the panel's chairperson.
The government is expected to bring the fresh delimitation bill alongside the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, which seeks to amend constitutional provisions to enable the implementation of the one-third quota for women after the first delimitation exercise following its commencement. The Union cabinet had cleared the revised legislation on Friday, ahead of the special sitting of Parliament.
However, the bill clarifies that after the nomination of an Election Commissioner as a member under the relevant clause, the nomination of an Election Commissioner as a member under will be made except to fill the casual vacancy of such member under section 6.
For Meghalaya and Nagaland, the third member will be a person nominated by the respective state governor. The bill also mentions the constituencies of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir under Pakistan's occupation. “The Election Commission shall act as delimitation commission for the purpose of delimiting constituencies in the Legislative Assembly of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir falling under the occupation of Pakistan, when the area of the Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir under the occupation of Pakistan ceases to be so occupied,” the bill states.
Delimitation commission to also include MPs, MLAs as associate members
The bill which is expected to be introduced in Parliament proposes that the delimitation commission will associate ten members from each state to assist it – five Lok Sabha MPs representing that state and five members of its legislative assembly. In states with five or fewer MPs, all such MPs will be associate members, and the total number of associated members will be reduced accordingly.
However the associate members will not have voting rights or the power to sign any decision of the commission. The MPs part of the panel will be nominated by the Lok Sabha speaker, while the speaker of the respective state legislative assembly will nominate the MLAs, keeping in mind the composition of the House concerned.
The panel can also seek assistance from the registrar-general and census commissioner, surveyor general, government officials geographical information system experts and other relevant individuals.
Also Read | How Centre's delimitation plan could change India's electoral map: A look at state-wise numbers
Term and functions of the delimitation commission
The term of the commission will be specified by the Centre through a notification if the Bill is passed and becomes an Act. The Union government can, on the request of the commission, extend its term “by such further period as it may consider necessary.”
The delimitation commission will readjust:
(a) the allocation of seats in the House of the People to the States and Union territories and the total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State, in accordance with the provisions of this Act;
(b) the division of each State and Union territory into territorial constituencies, on the basis of the latest census figures

Even as Christian communities continue to face attacks allegedly from Hindutva groups across various parts of West Bengal, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) state president Samik Bhattacharya on November 15 issued a warning to Christian missionary school, saying it they were found promoting “anti-India activities”, they would not be allowed to function.
“If any Christian missionary school, due to religious reasons, promotes anti-India activities, we will not let that school run,” he said while addressing a gathering at Birsa Munda’s birth anniversary celebrations in New Alipore, Kolkata.
“Guardians should become alert that an official at a school placed a Pakistani flag on the table of his chamber… in a school here in Kolkata. Please correct yourselves… We will let this happen in West Bengal no matter how powerful they are. All Christian missionaries can take to the streets; we are not opposed to any religion, but sitting in our state, in our country, we will not let you insult saffron [colour]… We will not allow it.”
Prior to issuing the warning, Bhattacharya claimed that a woman BJP worker was prevented from entering a “prestigious school in Kolkata” for wearing a saffron saree. “A prestigious school in Kolkata…I am not naming the school right now because a few days later I will sit outside its gates. One of our sisters, our BJP worker who was seen wearing saffron attire…was told [by the school] that ‘wearing these saris, you cannot come to school, you cannot pronounce the name of lotus flower while teaching the students.’ This is happening in the land of Kolkata where several eminent personalities have walked,” he said.
He further went on to insinuate that Christians were continuing to uphold British mentality in India. “It’s been 75 years since the British left the country, but the mentality has not left. You have come here; you are holding your establishments; you are Catholics, you are Protestants; you can propagate your religion. But remember, this government is not Babur’s government. This government is not trying to uphold British legacies. West Bengal has an independent government,” he said.
A report published by The Telegraph stated that the BJP president alleged that a reputed college in Kolkata was carrying out religious conversions in Asansol forcibly through “allurements”. “There is an obhijato (elite) college in Kolkata whose principal is carrying out religious conversion in Asansol. This cannot be allowed to continue. This is not the government of the Trinamool Congress, this is not the Left Front government…We are against political intervention in any educational institution. We want schools to create their own curriculum,” the report quoted him.
Bhattacharya, however, did not name any Christian missionary schools or colleges or provide any evidence behind the severe allegations he levelled against the community.
Upon being asked about Bhattacharya’s allegations against Christian missionaries, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on November 17, Tuesday, told the media, “…I get information on this and verify the facts. If the information is true and a written complaint is filed, if an individual did it, action will be taken against the individual; and if it was done institutionally, we will withdraw the NOC given to the institute.”

If the information is true and a written complaint is filed—if an individual did it, action will be taken against the individual; and if it was done institutionally…”

Christian Bodies Condemn Remarks, Issue Statements
The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba (BCP) in a statement on November 18 reacted to Bhattacharya’s statement saying “sweeping accusations without evidence” maligned a peace-loving community and endangered social harmony, and demanded “specific facts, accountability, and immediate legal action”.
BCP posed eight questions to Bhattacharya and the state administration, questioning the lack of legal action against alleged perpetrators of illegal conversion, if any, and the silence over recurring vigilante attacks on Christians. It asked why attacks and vandalism of prayer meetings by ‘militant groups’ had not been condemned, whether such groups were allegedly being used to intimidate Christians, and sought the status of FIRs filed in connection with alleged threats and attacks against the community in the state.

The BCP also demanded documentary evidence of alleged conversions in Christian-run educational institutions, pointing out that millions studied in these schools, and urged ruling party leaders educated in missionary institutions to share their experiences.
The association further questioned the administration’s silence on around 50 alleged attacks on Christian prayer gatherings over the past four to five months, contrasting it with their vocal responses to issues like an official allegedly displaying a Pakistani flag or wearing a saffron saree, without conclusive evidence.
Concerns Ahead of Christmas
Following Bhattacharya’s remarks, Paritosh Canning, moderator of the Church of North India and bishop of the Calcutta diocese, on Sunday sought chief minister Suvendu Adhikari’s intervention against the rising number of attacks against the Christian community in West Bengal. Issuing a statement under the banner of Bengal Christian Council, he urged Adhikari to take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and security of Christians, churches and places of worship, to uphold the constitutionally guaranteed right of practising one’s faith.
“Our concerns are not without reason. Reports of attacks, intimidation and disruption of Christian religious activities have emerged from several districts of Bengal…These reported incidents include attacks on priests, pastors and worshippers, vandalism of churches and crosses, disruption of prayer meetings, intimidation of Christian families and interference with religious activities,” the statement read.
“These developments have caused considerable anxiety and apprehension among members of the Christian community. West Bengal has traditionally been a land of communal harmony…With Christmas approaching, the apprehensions of the Christian community have become particularly serious…the prevailing atmosphere of insecurity has raised genuine concerns about whether Christians will be able to observe their religious services and celebrate Christmas without fear or disruption,” the statement added.
Condemning Bhattacharya’s remarks, representatives of BCP and the West Bengal Association of Christian Schools held a joint press conference on November 16, Monday. Representatives of the associations dismissed the allegations of forceful religious conversion as baseless. They demanded that Bhattacharya name the two institutes and provide evidence to back his claims against Christian missionaries.
ALSO READ: Another attack on a Christian family in Bengal: Woman alleges mob assault, desecration of Bible
“A viral video has recently come to our attention. While we cannot verify its authenticity at this moment, the remarks recorded in it feature four grave allegations: claims of widespread religious conversions, an accusation that a…principal is involved in conversion activities; an allegation regarding a person wearing a saffron sari coming to a school; and a sweeping insinuation that even though the British have left, Christian missionary school administrators continue to carry a ‘British mentality,” read a statement by the representatives.
“At a time when vigilantes and hooligans are taking the law into their own hands across various districts — vandalising and launching brutal attacks on peaceful prayer meetings under the false pretext of forced conversions and desperately trying to build a fabricated narrative — the Christian community is both shocked and deeply angered to hear such an incredible, hate-mongering and aggressive speech from a usually balanced and sagacious leader like Samik Babu,” it added.
Speaking to Alt News, Moloy D’Costa, secretary of the West Bengal Association of Christian Schools and vicar-general of the Roman Catholic archdiocese of Calcutta, said, “The comments made by Mr Bhattacharya are vague. Every school has its own dress code, and there is no universal colour code. The authorities should either provide evidence or identify specific institutions and take appropriate action against them, rather than making general statements that vilify an entire community and a network of institutions.”
D’Costa also pointed out, “Several leaders in the party attended Christian missionary institutions; have they converted to Christianity? Converting to Christianity is a lengthy process. Simply visiting a church or sprinkling water is not part of that process. Accusations of forced conversion are being made from all sides, yet not a single case has been reported where anyone has been proven guilty of such actions.”
National Christian Council (NCC) state general secretary Arpan Rana strongly condemned Bhattacharya’s remarks on Christian missionary institutions, stating that “sweeping allegations without evidence” risk fostering suspicion and hostility towards the Christian community.
Rana told Alt News that Christian institutions were primarily invested in “education, humanitarian service, moral development and nation-building, not forced religious conversion,” adding that students from diverse religious backgrounds have studied in these institutions without abandoning their faiths. “Thousands of students from Hindu, Muslim, Christian and other communities have received education from these institutions while preserving their respective religious identities,” he said.
He also termed the portrayal of Indian Christianity as a legacy of British colonialism ‘historically misleading’, noting that Christianity existed in India long before colonial rule. “We expect scholarly arguments backed by evidence, not broad political claims. If any institution is found to engage in unlawful conversion, we support impartial investigations, but the entire Christian community should not be collectively accused,” he added.
Akin to other Christian associations in the state, Rana, on behalf of the NCC, urged the state government to protect Christian institutions, churches and communities, and ensure they can celebrate Christmas peacefully.
As precautionary measures, the BCP also advised churches to inform local authorities about upcoming programmes, establish a community alert system, ring church bells thrice if suspicious groups enter church premises, immediately notify police, and install CCTV cameras at vulnerable points. It also urged members to seek legal aid from BCP, maintain discipline and peaceful conduct, refrain from retaliation, and involve neighbours of all faiths and civil society members in Christmas celebrations to foster communal harmony.
Alt News has been documenting instances of hate crimes against the Christian community in West Bengal since early this year. Instances of violence, attacks, vandalism, and intimidation have often been carried out by Right-wing groups including Bajrang Dal, Vishva Hindu Parishad, and others, against individuals practising Christianity, house churches, and small Christian communities. However, in most of the cases we have reported, police action has been sparse, with fresh instances of harassment emerging regularly.

Charles Leclerc seeking outlier as Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull try to catch Mercedes at Qatar Grand Prix
Mercedes dominated Friday's practice sessions at the Qatar Grand Prix and Charles Leclerc suggested Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull are missing something; watch final practice at 2.30pm ahead of Qualifying at 6pm on Saturday live on Sky Sports F1
Friday 27 November 2026 20:50, UK
Charles Leclerc believes an “outlier” has given Mercedes a “massive” advantage at the Qatar Grand Prix, after Kimi Antonelli and George Russell dominated Friday’s practice sessions.
Mercedes were nearly half a second quicker than the rest of the field at the Lusail International Circuit as Antonelli topped both sessions from Russell.
Their four-tenths advantage over closest challenger Lando Norris in second practice could have been even greater, with neither Antonelli nor Russell completing a full low-fuel lap on the soft tyres. It was an ominous sign for the rest of the field ahead of Saturday's qualifying, which gets under way at 6pm, with coverage live on Sky Sports F1 from 5.15pm.

Mercedes' dominance was similar to their pace advantage earlier in the season but the second half of 2026 has largely been very close between F1's top four teams - Mercedes, Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren.
Ferrari were over one second behind Antonelli on a dismal Friday as Leclerc spun in second practice and Lewis Hamilton suffered an engine problem which brought his Ferrari to a halt.
"Honestly it's been a very difficult day. It's not that we didn't try on the softs, we couldn't improve our lap time on the mediums," said Leclerc.
"I lost the car and had some damage so we had to repair the car but that was the first lap of FP2 and I couldn't improve and even on the new soft later on I couldn't improve.
"A very, very difficult day. The feeling is just very difficult to get right. Not even on high fuel we were strong, so for now, it looks like a very difficult weekend but we are working hard to try and understand something.
"For some reason, Mercedes are so much faster than everybody expected, so the gaps are just a little bit strange, so there's something that's an outlier and we just need to find that."
Ferrari were not expected to be strong at the Lusail International Circuit due to the long flat out zones and high-speed corners but Leclerc suggested his team, along with McLaren and Red Bull were missing a trick that will give them more pace.
"I don't think we know yet what's the outlier. I think other teams probably didn't find that because Mercedes still have a massive advantage," he said.
"We are going to work towards that and analyse the data to understand what's going on."
Norris: Mercedes not even worth thinking about
McLaren were predicted to be very competitive in Qatar due to their strength in the high-speed corners but Norris and Piastri were never close to matching the pace of Mercedes.
On Saturday, McLaren are expected to put the new floor they ran in Las Vegas on the car but Norris does not think it will make a big enouch difference to catch Mercedes who are in "a different category".
"I don't know how much that will help around here compared to Vegas," said last year's world champion.
"But obviously tonight [Friday] we will see how much we can gain from that. It's not going to be the gap we need.
"We are probably seven tenths off the Mercedes a lap so it's not even worth thinking about them. But relative to the rest we seem to be in a good place. The fact we can have the new floor on tomorrow will add a little bit and a little bit is better than nothing. We seem in a relatively decent place."
Both Antonelli and Russell pointed out that Verstappen will always be a threat and the four-time world champion is coy about his chances of challenging the Mercedes in qualifying.
"A bit of a difficult day. The balance of the car is a bit too disconnected at the moment to go fast, so that's what we need to fix," said the Red Bull driver.
"The all-round balance is not there at the moment and is costing us quite a bit of lap time. We will keep trying and see how good we can get it."
"Mercedes look quite far ahead on the short run and long run. Let's see how much we can close the gap."

Kobe – The Kobe Municipal Government on Friday submitted to the city assembly a draft ordinance to introduce a tax on vacant condominium units in central areas, aiming to reduce investment-driven vacancies and promote the effective use of housing.
If enacted, it would mark the first tax in Japan targeting vacant condominium units specifically. The city aims to introduce the tax in fiscal 2030.
The levy would be imposed on owners of units without resident registration in condominiums located in such central areas as the Sannomiya and Motomachi districts.
The tax would consist of 0.7% of a condominium unit’s assessed value plus an additional amount based on its location and floor area.
It would be collected as a non-statutory ordinary tax, whose revenue use is not restricted. Tax reductions or exemptions would be available when resident registration is temporarily absent due to relocation, inheritance or other reasons, or when the period since the unit was put on the rental market has not exceeded a year.
The city is concerned that purchases of condominium units for investment or asset-holding purposes are increasing the number of units without actual residents despite growing housing demand in central areas.
It set up an expert panel in 2025 to discuss measures for the proper management of condominiums.

The most successful team in the competition with three titles, Tamil Nadu has endured its fifth successive group-stage exit in the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) this season.
It won three of its seven matches and finished sixth among eight teams in Group B. The campaign exposed a reluctance to move beyond familiar personnel and approaches, even as modern T20 cricket demands greater intent, flexibility and tactical imagination. Tamil Nadu had a promising talent pool at its disposal but failed to utilise it optimally.
The decision to bat traditional opener N. Jagadeesan in the middle order once again proved counterproductive. Group-B topper Delhi, with its high-intent batting spine, posted five 200-plus totals in seven matches. Tamil Nadu managed just one. The side eventually brought in youngsters Andre Siddarth and Rithik Easwaran, whose positive intent offered a glimpse of what the team could build on.
Tamil Nadu’s decision to persist with Shahrukh Khan despite his disappointing previous season backfired. Though he began with an unbeaten 46 against Railways, he struggled to make an impact thereafter. His inability to see TN home against Punjab, with 38 needed off 36 balls, was in stark contrast to his peak. In the 2021-22 final against Karnataka, he had struck an unbeaten 33 off 15 balls, sealing Tamil Nadu’s third title with a last-ball six.
All-rounder Sunny Sandhu, who was part of the team that won the men’s U-23 State-A Trophy last season, wasn’t backed consistently. Known for his ability to swing the new ball, he was used in that role in the first two matches before not being called upon to bowl against Haryana. He was subsequently dropped for the next three games, only to return for the final match against Saurashtra, where he showcased his all-round ability, scoring 44 and picking up four wickets. Sonu Yadav, another all-rounder capable of swinging the new ball, did not find a place in the squad. Pacer Esakkimuthu, the breakout star of the previous TNPL season, was also overlooked.

Despite having a promising pool of young fast bowlers, Tamil Nadu relied on veterans Athisayaraj Davidson and R. Silambarasan, who leaked runs at economies of 11.83 and 13.12, respectively. India U-19 World Cup winner D. Deepesh, known for his pace, could have provided the hit-the-deck-hard option that the attack seemed to lack. There were other exciting prospects from the India U-19 circuit to invest in, including pacer Pranav Ragavendra and pace-bowling all-rounders R.S. Ambrish and V. Shavin.
Leg-spinner Jhathavedh Subramanyan, the breakout star of TNPL 2023, who was with Sunrisers Hyderabad (SRH) in the IPL, had to wait till the final match against Saurashtra to make his debut. His wrist-spin could have been a useful match-up option against Delhi, which had three left-handers in its top five, including Priyansh Arya, who smashed a record-breaking 181.

CA may not like sandpaper forum findings - Vaughan
- Published
Cricket Australia (CA) will not like what it finds from a forum into the sandpaper scandal, according to former England captain Michael Vaughan.
CA has invited evidence into the ball-tampering controversy of Australia's Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018 following weeks of speculation over which players and coaches were involved.
"It's very clear to me that Cricket Australia are going to find some things out that they're probably not going to want to find out," Vaughan told the Test Match Special podcast.
"If they don't release the truth of what they find in this forum out to the public, we're going to get back to square one."
The row over the ball-tampering scandal was reignited by claims published in the autobiography of former Australia batter Usman Khawaja.
At the time of the controversy, only batter Cameron Bancroft, then captain Steve Smith and his deputy David Warner were punished for the cheating plot.
Khawaja alleged all players and coaches knew of the tampering and should have taken responsibility, a testimony supported by Bancroft, Warner and squad players Chadd Sayers and Jon Holland.
Former coach Darren Lehmann and Australia captain Pat Cummins have been among those who have denied knowledge or involvement.
- Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes 
  - Published16 hours ago
In an attempt to calm the row that has engulfed Australian sport, CA has established a six-week forum for players, coaches and staff involved in 2018 to give evidence to senior counsel Fiona McLeod.
Although McLeod will publish her findings and CA will give a public response, evidence will remain confidential, there will be no new attribution of responsibility and no further sanctions.
The scope of the forum will extend to the Australian home season prior to the 2018 tour of South Africa, which included their 4-0 Ashes defeat of England.
Writing in his autobiography in 2019, former England opener and captain Sir Alastair Cook said the tourists had suspicions about how Australia were getting the ball to move, and that Warner later admitted to using substances attached to the strapping on his hands in domestic matches.
Cook's suspicions related to the third Test in Perth. Heavy overnight rain had delayed the fifth day at the Waca, when England were attempting to save the Test.
When play finally began, the outfield was wet, conditions that would normally prevent any reverse swing. Cook claimed that Australia found an "inordinate" amount of reverse.
Former England batter Dawid Malan was at the crease on the final morning and told BBC Sport: "The amount it did move on a wet day, maybe something was being done to get that ball moving.
"That's not me accusing anyone of doing it, but you look and think: 'Yeah, maybe there was something to get the ball moving that much on that last day'."
Left-hander Malan scored more runs - 383 - and faced more deliveries - 897 - than any other England batter in that series.
"You look back and think did the ball start reversing at any times? In some of the games we were probably guilty of not batting long enough for the ball to start reversing.
"The standout for me would have been that Perth Test, day five. It had rained quite a lot and there was a good little wet patch on the wicket. Batting in that innings, it was quite evident the ball was reversing. I'm not for one minute saying people were scratching the ball or putting anything on it.
"Whether or not they were tampering with the ball then is not my knowledge, but the ball was swinging a lot more in that series. Maybe, in hindsight, things had started then and they were trying to reverse it."
Asked about what the CA forum could uncover about the 2017-18 Ashes, Vaughan said: "From my cricket experience and a cynical look at the past of what may or may not have happened, I don't think Cricket Australia are going to like what they find.
"Do they make that all public? There's no way in a million years that more people didn't know something was happening to a ball."
Despite the potential implications for a series result against England, the England and Wales Cricket Board has not contacted CA about the forum and has no plans to do so.
Announcing the forum, CA chair David Boon said: "It is very important to understand that it will not seek to sanction or recriminate."
And Vaughan agreed that the governing body should not seek to impose new punishments.
"You can't go back and punish people," said Vaughan, who famously led England to victory in the 2005 Ashes. "The punishment was far too harsh for the three players at the time. Darren Lehmann lost his job as coach for Australia - there's four people who were really punished.
"The tampering of a ball is almost the smallest part of the story now.
"Some have said that they had no clue sandpaper was used. I understand that, they can have that opinion. The more different aspects of this story that come to light, the more there is that element of do you believe those people? You have to say I'm not too sure about that now."

Chloe Dang went to Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi airport at midnight, desperate for information about her missing husband.
Tran Hiep was supposed to land in Thailand on a flight from Cambodia on 19 September, and Dang had planned to meet him at the airport. He never arrived.
The previous morning, they had spoken about birthday celebrations for his family. His mother and niece had birthdays coming up, and the couple were discussing where to celebrate.
It was an entirely ordinary conversation, Dang tells The Independent. Nothing suggested anything was wrong.
A few hours later, she messaged him casually about something at their home. He did not respond. At first, she assumed he was busy with work or would reply after returning to his hotel.
By evening, she had still heard nothing.
“I thought maybe he got back to the hotel really late or something like that,” she says. “So, that was the last contact with him on 18 September.”
When Hiep didn’t arrive the following day at the airport where the Australian couple were supposed to meet, Dang reported him missing to local police, who directed her to the tourist police and immigration authorities.
She soon learned from the airline that Hiep had never boarded the flight. “My mental health just broke down,” she tells The Independent. But she still had a glimmer of hope that he would show up.
Hiep is a member of Viet Tan, an international pro-democracy organisation designated a “terrorist” group by Vietnam in 2016. Viet Tan was engaged in armed resistance against Vietnam’s communist government in the 1980s. It re-emerged in 2004 as a political party advocating non-violent change.
However, according to Human Rights Watch, Vietnamese authorities have continued to arrest and imprison its members.
Hiep, 51, has been involved in activism for more than 20 years.
For two days after Hiep disappeared, Dang did not tell his family. Eventually, she told his mother and sister. For the first six days, only the three women knew about his disappearance. They contacted his colleagues, the people he had met on the ground in Cambodia.
Nothing emerged.
Nearly 10 days later, Vietnamese authorities acknowledged that Hiep, Norwegian activist Nguyen Duc Thuan, and a Vietnamese national named Thai Cong Truong Son had been detained while attempting to cross into the country “illegally”.
Dang disputes the allegation. Hiep, an Australian citizen, had previously travelled to Vietnam on a visa, she said, while his Norwegian companion did not need one for trips of up to 45 days.
“Why would he enter Vietnam illegally when he could go legally?” she asked, describing the allegation as a pretext for their detention.
On 7 October, Cambodia’s interior ministry said Hiep and Thuan had entered the country, but there was no record of their departure. It “categorically” denied handing the two men over to Vietnamese authorities.
Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, described the disappearance of the activists as “apparent abduction”.
“The apparent abduction and detention of the foreign nationals raises many questions about the roles of both the Vietnamese and Cambodian governments,” she said in a statement then. “The Norwegian and Australian governments should press Vietnamese authorities to grant them immediate access to their nationals and to drop baseless charges against them.”
Hiep has since received two visits from Australian consular officials, on 15 October and 20 November, at a pretrial detention centre in Ho Chi Minh City.
He sent a message through the officials who visited him last month saying he was traumatised and struggling mentally. He denied crossing the border voluntarily or intending to enter Vietnam at all.
After the second visit, Dang received a more reassuring update about her husband’s physical condition. He was doing well and managing to look after himself, she said, although he remained traumatised.
Activists allege that Vietnam is intensifying its crackdown on Viet Tan and fellow dissident groups, restoring to arrests, trials in absentia, abductions, and pressure on foreign nations.
In 2019, Vietnamese authorities arrested Australian Viet Tan member Chau Van Kham and his local associates Nguyen Van Vien and Tran Van Quyen, and sentenced them to 12, 11 and 10 years in jail, respectively, on terrorism charges linked to their involvement with the group. Kham was released in July 2023, but Vien and Quyen remain imprisoned.
In 2018, they had arrested Le Quoc Binh in Binh Dinh province and accused him of working with Viet Tan and smuggling weapons from Cambodia to “carry out terrorist activities” in Vietnam.
Viet Tan rejected the allegations at the time, calling them “a ridiculous fabrication”.
Vietnamese security agencies have been accused of abducting dissidents in Germany and Thailand, including Trinh Xuan Thanh, Truong Duy Nhat, and Duong Van Thai.
In the past year, courts have tried several overseas nationals in absentia, convicting and sentencing them to lengthy prison terms.
Vietnam has also been accused of pressuring foreign nations like Thailand and Cambodia to return its citizens who have fled out of fear of arbitrary arrest, torture, or imprisonment.
“Being a human rights activist or helping people is not a crime,” Dang says. “You shouldn’t be punished for being a human rights activist or helping people.”
Vietnam currently holds more than 160 political prisoners, activists say, allegedly for exercising their right to free expression or advocating human rights and democracy. Dozens are in detention awaiting trial.
In the first nine months of 2026, Vietnamese courts sentenced 31 activists to lengthy prison terms, including bloggers Hoang Thi Hong Thai and Huynh Ngoc Tuan. In the same period, police allegedly arrested 46 people for criticising the government.
For a minute, when Dang forgets the serious allegations facing her husband and the torment of the last few months, she recalls a man who can be “cheeky” and “funny”.
His friends in Australia know him as someone who cracks jokes and makes everyone laugh, she says.
He loves music and plays the drums, guitar and keyboard. At gatherings, he often takes charge of the instruments while everyone else sings.
Hiep moved to Australia when he was 17. While still a student, he co-founded a group campaigning against human trafficking.
“He’s a normal man. He’s a good husband and also a good son to his family,” Dang tells The Independent.
Dang is now travelling across Europe to draw attention to his detention and seek international support for his release. She says the alleged abduction of her husband and the Norwegian activist is concerning.
“This time we are talking about Australians and Norwegians,” she says. “Next time it could be British, French, or anyone.”
She acknowledges the Australian government’s efforts to secure her husband’s release, not least the decision by prime minister Anthony Albanese to raise the case at the recent Asean summit in Manila.
“But it has been two months already in this case,” she says. “My husband got abducted, so I still want our government to do more to bring my husband back home safely soon.”
She calls for action to tackle transnational repression. “We have to do something to stop it because it’s not just my husband. There have been many other cases recently, involving a lot of other people.”
The Independent contacted Vietnam’s embassy in Canberra for comment, but didn’t get an immediate response.
In a statement earlier, the embassy rejected the allegation of abduction as “unfounded and misleading”, and maintained that the men were arrested as per the law.
Viet Tan said the “abduction” of the activists in Cambodia and “their subsequent imprisonment in Vietnam constitute a grave violation of international law”. “Democracies, most notably Australia and Norway, must not tolerate this type of transnational repression carried out by the Vietnamese authorities,” the group said in a statement.

Black Friday gives India’s ecommerce and D2C brands another opportunity to reach shoppers who held back during this year’s festive sales. But it also arrives much sooner after Diwali, leaving less room between two major spending occasions. Beginning today and running through Cyber Monday on November 30, the four-day Black Friday–Cyber Monday (BFCM) window falls just 19 days after Diwali. Last year, the gap was 39 days – more than twice as long. The tighter calendar follows a festive season in which online sales grew but fell short of expectations. Online sales rose an estimated 17% YoY to ₹1.41 Lakh Cr, falling short of Datum Intelligence’s ₹1.50–1.55 Lakh Cr forecast. Average online card payments fell 13%, while weaker smartphone sales weighed on overall growth. However, last year’s Black Friday performance gives brands reasons to pursue the opportunity. Daily gross merchandise value (GMV) on GoKwik’s network rose 42% during BFCM compared with the preceding 30 days. Unicommerce recorded around 27% YoY growth in Black Friday week orders, while Nykaa Fashion’s Pink Friday Sale drew 31 Mn visits and recorded 44% YoY growth in new customers. Replicating this momentum this year will mean finding demand beyond purchases consumers have already completed. Unlike the Thanksgiving and Christmas shopping cycle that anchors Black Friday in the US, India’s November sale window overlaps with winter purchases, wedding shopping, and year-end travel. These occasions give brands opportunities to clear inventory, acquire customers, and strengthen recall before the new year. This year, however, Black Friday follows Diwali much more closely, making it harder to persuade shoppers to buy again, particularly in categories they have already spent on. The Post-Diwali Demand Challenge For brands, running successive sales also means coordinating inventory, fulfilment, and marketing campaigns within a tighter window. Devangshu Dutta, founder of Third Eyesight and cofounder of PVC Partners, said large retailers need predictable demand patterns to manage their supply chains and customer-facing operations. Retailers have adopted additional shopping occasions beyond traditional Indian festivals to generate demand across the year. But another sale does not guarantee another purchase. Deepankar Madaan, vice-president, business, at D2C enablement platform Velocity, said consumers have become increasingly value-conscious. While shoppers may wait for events such as Black Friday to make high-ticket purchases, lower-value products need a clear utility proposition to stand out from routine promotions. He put typical D2C order values at around ₹1,100-₹1,200. He expects post-Diwali wallet fatigue to limit repeat buying within the same category. “Consumers who already bought products during Diwali are highly unlikely to buy the exact same type of product from a competing brand during Black Friday. If they shop at all, it will be for an entirely different product category,” he said. Frequent promotions also risk making consumers less willing to pay full price. Harminder Sahni, founder of Wazir Advisors, described Black Friday as a retailer-led phenomenon, with businesses continually seeking occasions to generate shopping interest. “There is always some sale around the corner, so consumers don’t see much reason to pay full price and rather wait,” Sahni said. This year’s festive sales also left brands with shoppers who browsed but held back on expensive purchases. Black Friday offers another opportunity to brands to convert that interest into sales, although the shorter gap after Diwali could limit repeat purchases from customers who have already spent. Finding The Next Purchase For Mani Singhal, MD and co-leader of the consumer and retail practice at Alvarez & Marsal India, brands’ Diwali sales data should guide whom they target and which products they discount. “... put more of the budget behind customers who browsed and didn’t buy, or are due to replenish, and concentrate discounts on products where a lower price is likely to change the purchase decision. The right choice depends on whether the brand needs to release cash tied up in stock, recruit new customers or bring existing ones back,” Singhal said. This approach would distinguish shoppers with an outstanding need from those being encouraged to stock up through another discount. The sales channel could also influence how brands structure their offers. Soumen Samanta, founding member and CBO at travel accessories brand Escape Plan, said festive sales around Diwali are characterised by intense marketplace competition and deep price cuts. Black Friday, in his assessment, offers greater scope to generate demand through brands’ own D2C websites. Product bundles can help increase average order value (AOV) and protect gross margins without relying on deeper discounts, he said. Samanta also sees November’s travel demand as an opportunity to introduce products and offers. Brand websites entered the BFCM event after recording stronger festive order growth than marketplaces. According to Datum Intelligence’s report, citing Unicommerce, GoKwik, and ClickPost data, brand website orders grew 27–30%, compared with 8% for marketplaces. Acquisition costs could offer some relief during the Black Friday push. Samanta said digital customer acquisition becomes cheaper in late November after Amazon and Flipkart’s peak festive advertising campaigns end. In his assessment, lower acquisition costs and product bundles can improve Black Friday’s economics for D2C brands. For this year’s event, however, the benefit will depend on whether these campaigns convert shoppers and how much discounting is needed to secure their orders. Deferred purchases, replenishment, and winter and travel needs offer routes to another sales peak. With the shorter gap between the two sales, the test is whether brands can convert customers’ needs into additional business without borrowing too heavily from December’s orders.

The Union Cabinet on Friday has cleared a new women's reservation bill linked to delimitation which proposes a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats in all states.
This bill is likely to be brought before the special sitting of the Parliament which is set to begin next week.
The Union Cabinet gave its nod to the new bill with amendments in order to ensure no state loses its share of representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to others after the delimitation exercise is carried out, PTI reported citing sources.
Quick answers to key questions
It proposes increasing Lok Sabha strength from 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The Cabinet-approved proposal also says every state would receive a similar increase in seats.
The proposal is reported to use the 2011 Census to redraw the increased number of seats.
The proposed freeze is intended to keep state representation from changing again until 2051. The government says the uniform increase is meant to address concerns about states losing their relative share of Lok Sabha seats.
Southern states have recorded slower population growth than several northern states, raising concern that population-based delimitation could reduce their relative representation. The proposed uniform increase is intended to address those concerns.
The government says increasing the number of seats would help implement the 33% women's reservation in Parliament and state assemblies ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha election.
The bill also proposes a freeze on the number of seats till 2051, with the sources telling PTI that the uniform 51 per cent increase has been mandated in order to address the concerns southern states have expressed earlier.
The new bill is reportedly using the 2011 Census in order to redraw the increased seats.
If this proposed amendment passes, India will see an increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats from 543 to a maximum of 850 through delimitation.
The government's opinion is that this move will allow for the implementation of the 33 per cent quota for women in the Parliament as well as state assemblies ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.
The government has called for a four-day special sitting -- November 30 and December 1 in Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in Rajya Sabha.
"When the government calls a session or a special session, that means there are very important bills or business for the nation," Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said, as per PTI.
The opposition INDIA bloc is against the legislation and will be meeting on Saturday to discuss its strategy.
Non-INDIA bloc parties like the DMK, AAP, and the BJD have also been invited for the meeting, PTI reported citing sources.
Speaking with reporters, Congress general secretary in-charge organisation K C Venugopal said, "PM (Narendra) Modi and (Home Minister) Amit Shah want to set a big trap against the people of India. That is the design of this entire episode."
Notably, Supriya Sule of the NCP(SP) has said that she will not be attending the meeting since her father, party patriarch Sharad Pawar, is unwell. This comes amid buzz that the NCP(SP) might decide to side with the BJP on the delimitation issue.
MK Stalin has warned that under no circumstances should the 7.18 per cent seat share of Tamil Nadu in the Lok Sabha should be reduced.
"No change in position, no compromise, the DMK will never compromise on Tamil Nadu's interests; nor will it depart from its principles," Stalin said in a statement.
Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) Rajya Sabha MP Mahua Majhi questioned how the government could proceed with the bill without any update data, accusing the ruling party of renewed attempts of political poaching.
"If they don’t even have the necessary data, how can they carry out a delimitation exercise? This suggests that the politics of poaching has begun once again. We have several apprehensions regarding this: a session was called for just a single day,” Majhi told ANI.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut slammed the proposed bill on Friday, calling it “anti-national and anti-democratic”
“Realising they are set to lose in 2029, they have devised a new ploy: they intend to bring in 860 MPs and carry out a delimitation exercise. This bill is anti-national and anti-democratic; it must be opposed. Those who vote in favour of this bill will be traitors to the nation. Their names will be recorded in history as traitors,” Raut was quoted as saying by ANI.
